Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is filed praying that in the circumstances stated in the affidavit filed therewith, the High Court may  be pleased to issue a appropriate writ, Order or direction, particularlya Writ of Mandamus declaring action of the respondent Nos: 3 to 5 in trying to dispossessing the petitioner from his land admeasuring Ac.0.17 cents in survey No 115/B-2A and Ac.0.20 cents in No 115/B-3A of Nagireddypalle Revenue Village, Peddamudiam Mandal, YSR Kadapa District, without there being survey any land acquisition proceedings or any recourse to law, without invoking the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Rehabilitation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Resettlement Act, 2013, as illegal, irregular,
unjust, high handed besides arbitrary and violative of Articles 14 and 21 of Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondent Nos: 3 to 5 not to form any road from petitioner's land admeasuring Ac.0.17 cents in survey No 115/B-2A and Ac.0.20 cents in survey No 115/B-3A of Nagireddypalle Revenue Village, Peddamudiam Mandal, YSR Kadapa District, without there being any land acquisition proceedings or any recourse to law.

sentences.text: lA NO: 1 OF 2026  Petition under Section 151 CPC is filed praying that in the circumstances stated in the affidavit filed in support of the petition, the High Court may be pleased to direct the respondent Nos:3 to 5 not to form any road from petitioner's land Ac.0.17 cents in survey No: 115/B-2A; and Ac.0.20 cents in survey No: 115/B-3A of Nagireddypalle Revenue Village, Peddamudiam Mandal, YSR Kadapa District, without there being any land acquisition proceedings or any recourse to law.
Pending disposal of WP 393 of 2026, on the file of the High Court.

The petition coming on for hearing, upon perusing the Petition and the affidavit filed in support thereof and upon hearing the arguments of M/s. KODATI RAMYA KRISHNA Advocate for the Petitioner, GP FOR REVENUE for the Respondent Nos.1,2, 4 & 5; GP for Land Acquisitionfor the Respondent No.3, the Court made the following.

ORDER On perusal of the documents filed along with the writ petition, it shows that the land is in the name of the petitioner and now, the respondents are trying to dispossess the petitioner by laying a road without following due process of law.
Accordingly, there shall be a direction to the respondents not to dispossess the petitioner from the subject land without following due process of law.
